# kreiseck_validator

> Zero-dependency Dart package to validate, normalize and pretty-format common
> user input: email, phone, URL, host, IBAN, credit-card, license plate, IMEI,
> ICCID, MAC address, VIN and postal code. Global phone support, DACH-aware
> elsewhere. Apache-2.0. By Kreiseck Software Solutions (https://kreiseck.com).

Package name: `kreiseck_validator` (Dart, pub.dev). A TypeScript port ships as
`@kreiseck/validator` (npm) from the same repository. No runtime dependencies, no
network calls, no telemetry. Every algorithm (Luhn, ISO 13616 IBAN Mod-97, E.164
phone parsing, Damerau/OSA typo distance) is hand-written in pure Dart. Works on
all Dart and Flutter platforms. SDK: >=3.0.0 <4.0.0.

## Install

```
dart pub add kreiseck_validator
```

```dart
import 'package:kreiseck_validator/kreiseck_validator.dart';
```

## API

Twelve types, each a class with static methods. The common core is
`isValid` / `validate` / `normalize` / `format` (+ `tryFormat`), and every type has
`fieldDescriptor` / `formatPartial`. Nine also have `parse`, returning a structured
info object or null. `Email` is the one gap: it has no `format`/`tryFormat`/`parse`,
because a valid address has no canonical display form beyond `normalize`. Options
are named parameters, identical across all methods of a type.

- `Email` — pragmatic syntax check, `normalize` = trim + lowercase (never throws,
  does not validate), and `validate` attaches an offline typo-domain `Suggestion`
  (`user@gmial.com` -> suggests `user@gmail.com`). No `format`, no `parse`.
- `Phone({Country? country})` — E.164 for **every country** (libphonenumber-derived
  metadata), tolerant of `+43 (0)…`; `format(..., {bool international = true})`;
  `parse -> PhoneInfo`; `type -> PhoneNumberType` (classification data exists for
  AT only, everything else returns `unknown`).
- `Url({String defaultScheme = 'https'})` — scheme/host/TLD plausibility;
  `normalize` adds the scheme and lowercases the host; `format` is a compact
  display form (no scheme, no `www.`, no trailing slash).
- `Host` — bare hostname (RFC 1123), IPv4 or IPv6, optional port; `parse -> HostInfo`.
  More lenient than `Url`: no scheme required, accepts `localhost` and IP literals.
  ASCII only — no IDNA/punycode.
- `Iban({String? country})` — Mod-97 checksum plus per-country length from bundled
  metadata; `format` groups in 4s; `parse -> IbanInfo` (bank/branch/account codes,
  plus bank name + BIC for AT/DE/CH); `IbanCountry.of(iso2)` exposes per-country
  length, field layout and a valid example.
- `CreditCard` — Luhn plus network-aware length; `network(String) -> CardNetwork?`
  (Visa/Mastercard/Amex/Discover); `format` groups Amex 4-6-5, otherwise 4-4-4-4.
- `LicensePlate({String? country})` — grammar + region tables for AT, DE, CH, HR, TR;
  `parse -> PlateInfo` (district code, official region name, serial) with
  best-effort `PlateType` classification (diplomatic, authority, historic, …).
- `Imei({bool allowSv = false})` — 15-digit Luhn; `allowSv` also accepts a 16-digit
  IMEISV (no Luhn); `parse -> ImeiInfo`.
- `Iccid` — ITU-T E.118: MII plus Luhn on 20-digit cards (19-digit cards carry no
  check digit); `parse -> IccidInfo` resolves the issuing country from the
  embedded calling code.
- `MacAddress({MacNotation notation = MacNotation.colon, bool upperCase = false})` —
  EUI-48/64 in colon, hyphen, Cisco-dot and bare notation; `parse -> MacInfo`.
- `Vin` — ISO 3779 structure (17 chars, `I`/`O`/`Q` forbidden); `parse -> VinInfo`
  with the check-digit result and decoded model year.
- `PostalCode({required String country})` — curated patterns for 51 countries
  (Europe + Turkey) and canonical spacing (`1234AB` -> `1234 AB`); `parse -> PostalInfo`.
  The country is required: a bare postal code is ambiguous across countries.

### Input fields

`fieldDescriptor` and `formatPartial` exist on every type, taking the same options
as `validate`:

- `fieldDescriptor(...) -> FieldDescriptor` with `keyboard` (`KeyboardType`),
  `autofill` (`AutofillHint?`), `capitalization` (`Capitalization`), `maxLength`
  (`int?`, the length of the FORMATTED text), `example` (`String?`) and
  `allowedChars` (`String?`, a regex character-class body). Platform-neutral — no
  Flutter or DOM types; README.md carries the Flutter/HTML mapping tables.
- `formatPartial(...) -> String` — as-you-type formatting. Never throws. For the
  nine grouping types it produces exactly what `format` produces once the value is
  valid. `Email` and `Url` return the input unchanged and `Host` only filters and
  truncates, because their `format` is a display transform (or absent) and applying
  it mid-typing would delete what the user is typing.
- `example` is null wherever no verified real value exists — for most postal
  countries and for every phone country. Nothing is invented.
- `LicensePlate.maxLength` is null for every country: the AT grammar accepts an
  unbounded serial, so any cap could reject a plate `validate` accepts.

Result model:
- `sealed class ValidationResult` = `Valid(String normalized, {List<Suggestion> suggestions})` | `Invalid(List<ValidationIssue> issues)`
- `ValidationIssue(IssueCode code, String message)` — `IssueCode` is a stable, switchable, translatable enum; message is an English default.
- `Suggestion(String value, String reason)` — e.g. reason `'typo-domain'`.
- `class Country` — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 `iso2`, `callingCode`, display name and
  phone metadata for 245 regions; `Country.fromIso2` / `Country.fromCallingCode`.
- `isValid(x)` == `validate(x) is Valid`.

## Key behaviors / gotchas

- Phone national input (no leading `+`) REQUIRES `country:`; otherwise `Invalid(IssueCode.phoneAmbiguousCountry)`.
- An unresolvable calling code yields `Invalid(IssueCode.phoneUnknownCountry)`.
- `format`/`normalize` throw `FormatException` on invalid input — EXCEPT `Email.normalize`, which never throws.
- `fieldDescriptor` and `formatPartial` never throw, not even for an unknown
  country: they degrade to a generic descriptor. The error belongs to `validate`,
  which reports `postalUnknownCountry` / `plateUnknownCountry` for the same input.
- No DNS/MX/network lookups anywhere; the email typo hint is a purely local edit-distance heuristic.

## Cross-language consistency

Expected results are stored as language-agnostic JSON test vectors in `test/vectors/`
(one file per type, plus `field_descriptor.json` and `format_partial.json`).
`test/vectors_test.dart` checks Dart against them and the npm port's conformance
specs load the same files, so the two implementations cannot drift.
